name: Kadmiel
overview: Kadmiel was a male Levite known for his role in standing on the Levites' platform and exhorting the people of Israel to bless the Lord, as recorded in Nehemiah 9:4-5. He is also mentioned among the signatories of the sealed covenant document in Nehemiah 10:9. His active participation highlights his dedication to leading Israel in worship and covenant faithfulness.
namesAndTitles: The name Kadmiel means '[stand] before G-d [El],' reflecting a posture of reverence and service before God. This proper name, recorded in Nehemiah 9:4, does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries significant spiritual connotation tied to his role.
familyAndRelationships: Kadmiel is explicitly identified as a descendant of Levi, aligning him with the priestly tribe responsible for religious duties among Israel. Scripture does not record any additional family relationships beyond this tribal affiliation.
scriptureSignificance: Kadmiel's significance lies in his leadership role among the Levites during a critical moment of national repentance and renewal. By standing on the Levites' platform and calling Israel to bless the Lord, he helped guide the people in worship and recommitment to God's covenant. His inclusion among the sealed document's signatories further underscores his commitment to upholding the community's covenant obligations.
